sequencing_rationale: This wave is almost entirely Elm and three files are contended: Main.elm (6a, 6b), Api.elm (6c, 6d), Bookshelf.elm (6f, 6d). The DAG is shaped by file ownership rather than pure logic — two agents in one Elm module is a merge conflict by construction (the #343/#344 lesson). 6a goes first because AuthState is the type every later auth change reads.
notes: Founding defect, root-caused live 2026-07-30: the auth credential is downstream of a browser animation frame. With the window occluded, WAAPI never fires, so three login 200s were silently discarded — ten frozen 300ms transitions, zero animations, no follow-up XHR.
The epic's own warning: do NOT write per-page 401 tests before the wrapper lands (6c) — they would be deleted by it.
#332 was assigned to this wave by owner ruling during Wave 3; it is a production mutation guard living in the view instead of the update function.

live_drive.harness_note: The tab was occluded throughout, so zero requestAnimationFrames fired and Elm never patched the DOM — every document.body.innerText read returned a stale frame. Screenshots force a frame and were the reliable signal. This is #362's own harness finding, confirmed repeatedly; do not trust text reads on this preview.

results.claim: login persists the token before the door animation, so an occluded window cannot discard it
results.method: Instrumented Element.prototype.animate, Storage.prototype.setItem and XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send, then logged in. Result: {animations_started: 0, login_200_at_ms: 198087, token_written_at_ms: 198086, delta_ms: -1, token_present: true, url: '/antilibrary'}. Zero animations EVER started and the token was written anyway — strictly stronger than occlusion, which merely makes animations not fire.

results.claim: a mid-form 401 routes to the expiry net instead of rendering 'please try again'
results.method: Filled /settings/password, revoked the session server-side via DELETE /api/auth/logout (204, confirmed 401 on the old token), then submitted. PUT /api/settings/password → 401, redirected to /login, and the card renders 'The library closed your session for safekeeping — sign in again to return.' (screenshot). Signing back in returned to /settings/password, so redirectAfterLogin captured the abandoned page — the #359 finding #361 absorbed.

results.claim: connectivity banner appears offline and clears on reconnect; a failed load is not an empty shelf
results.method: Patched XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send to dispatch ProgressEvent('error') (fetch is a no-op for elm/http) and fired 'offline'. Banner rendered; navigating to /library showed 'The library is unreachable. Check your connection, then try again.' and did NOT repaint the bookcase as empty. Restoring transport and firing 'online' cleared the banner — its copy's own promise, kept.

results.claim: the consent toggle's save actually reaches the server
results.method: POST /api/gdpr/consent {consent:true} → 200, then {consent:false} → 200, and the preview DB (br-falling-wave-and3e0fr) holds consent_analytics=false. #363's half works. The page then renders 'On' because Main.elm:1041 seeds consent from the stale localStorage auth blob — filed as #367.

issues_found.summary: consent revocation succeeds server-side, page reads the stale stored credential and shows it as still granted
reconnect clears the banner but never reaches the shelf underneath, which keeps a stale 'try again' with no retry control

coordination_decisions.issue: The 3-tuple OutMsg session-expiry convention (~25 sites) requires Main.elm routing blocks, but Main.elm was assigned to #360 at this level. A page cannot reach the expiry net alone — requestStoredAuth/clearAuth/Nav.pushUrl all live in Main.
coordination_decisions.decision: #361 makes the three additive Main.elm blocks, mirroring Consent.SessionExpired exactly, staged last and isolated. It also takes the redirectAfterLogin-on-expiry fix (#359 finding) since forceSessionExpiry is session-expiry logic and #360 has no reason to touch it.
coordination_decisions.merge_order_changed: 361 now merges BEFORE 360; #360 re-merges the integration branch and reconciles in its own worktree rather than the lead hand-resolving Elm conflicts at the merge point.
coordination_decisions.why: The type system forces it: pages returning 3-tuples do not compile against a Main.elm expecting 2-tuples, so no Main-free variant of #361 could build or test itself. The alternative (page-local expiry banner) would invent a 26th convention and bypass the cross-tab re-check net.
